newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: IBCA gives Gensec strong domestic ratings.
newsitem.headline: IBCA gives Gensec strong domestic ratings.

text.p: International rating agency IBCA said on Monday it had given Genbel Securities (Gensec) a domestic short-term rating of A1 and a long-term A grade.

An IBCA statement said the ratings showed Gensec had the highest capacity for timely repayment in the short-term, supported by a strong capacity for timely repayment and a low expectation of investment risk in the long term.
However, it said adverse changes in business, economic or financial conditions might increase this investment risk.

"The ratings reflect the sound financial profile of Gensec," IBCA said, adding that the group's primary business included equity underwriting and primary market making, securities trading, treasury and investment asset management.

The unbundling and separate listing of Gensec in May last year had given the company new-found independence which was underpinned by a well capitalised balance sheet and new shareholder status, IBCA said.
The dominance of South African life assurance giant, Sanlam, which holds a 44 percent stake, was likely to impact positively on Gensec's future.
Although securities trading had traditionally been the revenue mainstay, Gensec's focus had shifted increasingly towards equity underwriting and structured finance and financial engineering.
"(The) group's revenue streams will change accordingly and its business profile evolve towards an investment banking operation," IBCA said, adding that Gensec would soon apply for a banking licence.

IBCA said management of market risk was a major concern in the uderlying risk profile, given the high exposure to equities and particularly as gearing was used extensively to leverage the trading portfolio.
However, capital was adequately insulated against dramatic market slumps, as indicated by an equity to assets ratio of 54.25 percent on a marked to market basis at the June 30, 1996 year-end.
